AWS Generative AI Offering

Generative AI on AWS: a layered view of models, agents, knowledge and governance built around Amazon Bedrock.

Browse all five slides

Understand the stack, then choose an entry point

This presentation organizes the AWS generative AI ecosystem into layers, from infrastructure and models to knowledge, agent services, governance and user experiences. It then explores model access, agent construction and the entry points presented for employees, application builders and software teams.

Source edition: November 2026. Product names, model lists, release dates, support dates and pricing statements are reproduced from the supplied deck; this page is a presentation conversion, not an independently verified service catalog.

Amazon Bedrock: Models and Deployment

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Generative AI on AWS · Amazon Bedrock Amazon Bedrock: one API, many providers 100+ models from about 18 providers Anthropic · OpenAI · Amazon Nova · Meta · Mistral · DeepSeek · Qwen · Google Gemma · NVIDIA · Cohere · Moonshot Amazon Nova 2 • AWS's own model family, launched December 2025 • Nova 2 Lite: fast, low-cost reasoning over text, images and video • Nova Sonic for real-time speech; Nova Forge to train your own Nova variant Frontier and open models • Anthropic Claude, including the Claude 5 models • OpenAI GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4 and Codex (GA June 2026) at OpenAI's own prices • Open weights: gpt-oss, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Qwen and more Ways to deploy On-demand pay per token Provisioned reserved throughput Custom Model Import bring your own weights SageMaker AI self-managed endpoints 3
Back to slide navigation

Slide 4 of 5

Building Agents: Runtime, Knowledge and Safety

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Generative AI on AWS · Amazon Bedrock Building agents: runtime, knowledge and safety Bedrock AgentCore Where agents run • Generally available since October 2025 • Modular: Runtime, Memory, Gateway, Identity, Observability, Policy • Managed harness (GA June 2026): define and run an agent in two API calls • Works with Strands, LangGraph or CrewAI and any model Knowledge Bases What agents know • Managed RAG: ingestion, chunking, embeddings and retrieval • Sources such as Amazon S3 and SharePoint • Vector stores including OpenSearch and Aurora • Callable as a tool from AgentCore agents Bedrock Guardrails What keeps them safe • Content filters, denied topics, PII redaction, prompt-attack detection • Automated Reasoning checks verify answers against your policy rules • One set of guardrails across every Bedrock model • Also evaluates agent actions in AgentCore Migration note: Amazon Q Developer IDE plugins end support on April 30, 2027 — Kiro is the successor. 4

Slide 5 of 5

Governance and Entry Points

Open hosted slide

Read slide text
Generative AI on AWS · Amazon Bedrock Governing it, and choosing where to start Trust and governance Familiar AWS controls IAM, KMS encryption, PrivateLink and CloudTrail apply to every model, including OpenAI and Anthropic Guardrails on every model One policy for content, PII and prompt attacks, plus Automated Reasoning checks for rule-bound answers Agent policy and identity AgentCore Policy sets which tools an agent may call (Cedar); Identity manages its credentials Evaluate and observe AgentCore Evaluations scores agent quality; OpenTelemetry traces plug into your existing monitoring Which entry point? Amazon Quick Employees, no code. An AI assistant that connects to work apps and takes action. Bedrock + AgentCore Builders, pro-code. Any model, your own data, custom apps and agents. Kiro Software teams. Spec-driven agentic development in the IDE and CLI. Pricing: pay as you go. Per-token or provisioned model pricing, plus usage-based charges for AgentCore, Knowledge Bases and Guardrails. 5

Frequently asked questions

What does this AWS generative AI presentation cover?

The five-slide deck maps the AWS generative AI stack across experiences, governance, agents, knowledge and tools, models and infrastructure.

How does the deck organize an agent application?

It separates runtime and agent services, retrieval through Knowledge Bases, model access through Bedrock, and governance through guardrails, policy, identity and observability.

Which entry points does the presentation compare?

The source deck compares Amazon Quick for employee experiences, Bedrock with AgentCore for custom applications, and Kiro for software development.

Are the model lists and product dates independently verified here?

No. This page reproduces the supplied November 2026 presentation. Model availability, product names, pricing and lifecycle dates are source-deck claims and should be checked against AWS documentation before implementation.
